$comment: Single source of truth for the OpenHands gateway tier profiles
(omniroute-t*-*.json + litellm-t*-*.json): the selectable models.
IDS RENAMED 2026-09-23: tier1 -> t1-orchestrator, tier2 -> t2-worker,
tier3 -> t3-driver, rag -> t4-rag. Delete the retired profile files
from ~/.openhands/profiles on next start (sync only writes).
OmniRoute tiers address combos on :20128 with the openai/ LiteLLM
transport prefix OpenHands requires (without it: provider-not-provided).
LiteLLM tiers address the static fallback on :4000 by its tier
model_names; they ALSO carry the openai/ prefix, which the OpenHands
litellm client stack strips before the HTTP call (measured 2026-09-22:
bare openai/t2-worker to the gateway 401s as an unknown provider, while
the proven openai/t1-orchestrator profile round-trips - so the wire
always carries the bare tier name the :4000 proxy defines). base_url is
container-side (host.docker.internal); the installer substitutes the
host-side URL nowhere - these profiles only ever run inside the container.
Costs stay 0: billing happens at the gateway, not per profile.
NO KEYS HERE: api_key is injected at install/start time from env
(AUTOOS_OMNIROUTE_KEY for omniroute-*, LITELLM_MASTER_KEY or
AUTOOS_LITELLM_API_KEY for litellm-*) or configuration/api-keys.yml
(omniroute:) / configuration/litellm/.env (master key).
Consumers: lib/**/install.* embedded setup (reads this file, never
inlines tiers), tools/sync-openhands-profiles.py (regenerates user
profiles; run by start-stack on every openhands start), both suites.
max_input_tokens / max_output_tokens of the omniroute-/litellm- tiers are
a generated copy of catalog/ide-models.json (the single source for
model windows and per-surface membership): edit the catalog and run
python3 tools/sync-ide-models.py, which also checks that this spec and
the catalog's openhands surface list the same models.
NOTE: OmniRoute gateway combos (omniroute-*) do NOT expose the full
reasoning effort variant ladder (minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh) because
the metadata (supportedThinkingEfforts) is absent from the gateway.
Use the direct OpenRouter profile (openrouter-muse-spark-1.3-contributor)
for full effort control. Requires OPENROUTER_API_KEY.
ORDER IS THE PUSH PRIORITY (reordered 2026-09-25): the OpenHands app keeps
at most 10 profiles and tools/sync-openhands-profiles.py --push-url fills
them in this order, removing lower-ranked AutoOS profiles to make room
and deleting retired ones. The top 10: the t1 -> t2 -> t3 hierarchy
(t1 first: it seeds the app settings and every agent profile's
llm_profile_ref), t2-orchestrator (small-scope orchestration), the
no-training -clean worker and driver (t1-clean's leg trains, so these two
are the privacy picks), t4-rag (grounded QA - nothing else does it),
opus-4-6 (frontier reasoning), gemini-3.8-flash (fast, free-first) and
t2-worker-free-only (zero spend). Below the line: deepseek (already a
t2 leg), t3-free-only, t1-clean and spark (the same spark legs as t1 -
in OpenHands the zen promo 403s, so all three answer alike), the direct
OpenRouter spark (needs its own key; OpenHands pins one effort, so the
ladder buys nothing), the LiteLLM fallbacks, and last the two
t1-free-only profiles: red by design outside OpenCode (their only leg is
the zen free promo, which answers 403 there).
retired_ids: profile ids this spec listed before the 2026-09-23 rename
(git log of this file), pushed before the sync kept a record of the
names it pushed. The push deletes an app profile only when it is in
that record (profiles/.autoos-pushed.json) or in retired_ids - never
because its name merely starts with omniroute-/litellm-/openrouter-.
